key_insight: Finite-energy bosonic codes let one oscillator sense an external force while protecting an unknown logical qubit, separating the force signal from logical information.
engineering_relevance: The approach could combine force sensing and recoverable quantum memory in superconducting hardware without dedicating separate oscillator modes to each task.
method: Encode logical amplitudes across discrete wave-packet sites and store the force signal in a shared internal coordinate.
Read out the endpoint probe independently of the logical state under continuous photon loss.
Apply binomial site recovery to correct logical errors and packet-dependent probe distortions.
evidence_signal: For a (2r+2)-packet code, the abstract reports memory infidelity of O(γ^(r+1)) and residual memory–probe correlations of O(γ^(r+2)), plus superconducting-circuit benchmarks with photon-number dephasing and Kerr nonlinearity.
watch_item: Hardware performance depends on competing dephasing and Kerr effects; the abstract does not establish experimental realization.
paper_title: Force Sensing in a Recoverable Bosonic Quantum Memory
